reconstructed_words.reasoning: The LXX participle διαγγέλλων reflects ספר in Piel ('declare/recount'), a standard equivalence (cf. Ps 9:15; 21:23 LXX). The translator likely read אֶל as a preposition governing חֹק, rendering the phrase as 'proclaiming the decree of the Lord.' πρόσταγμα regularly translates חֹק (cf. Ps 80:5 LXX).

alternatives.note: A participial form would more naturally yield διαγγέλλων, but the cohortative אֲסַפְּרָה is defensible since LXX often levels verbal forms.

reconstructed_words.reasoning: The LXX includes an explicit subject κύριος, which is absent in MT. This may reflect a Vorlage with יהוה repeated as subject of אָמַר, or it may be a translator's clarifying addition since MT's syntax leaves the speaker implicit. The doubling of κύριος is striking and suggests a possible Hebrew variant.

alternatives.note: The doubled κύριος could be a translator's gloss to disambiguate the speaker without a Vorlage variant.

reconstructed_words.reasoning: Direct equivalence: בְּנִי = υἱός μου and אַתָּה = εἶ σύ, with the explicit copula εἶ supplied per Greek syntax. This is standard LXX rendering of nominal clauses.
Word-for-word correspondence: אֲנִי = ἐγώ, הַיּוֹם = σήμερον, יְלִדְתִּיךָ = γεγέννηκά σε. The Greek perfect γεγέννηκα accurately renders the Hebrew qatal of ילד.

summary_technical: The Vorlage largely matches MT, with standard LXX equivalences (ספר=διαγγέλλω, חֹק=πρόσταγμα, ילד=γεννάω). The principal divergence is the doubled κύριος, which may reflect a Hebrew Vorlage with יהוה repeated as the subject of אָמַר, or alternatively a translator's clarification. No extant DSS witness preserves Ps 2:7 to adjudicate.
summary_plain: The Greek translator's Hebrew text was very close to the standard Masoretic Text. The one notable difference is that the Greek says 'the Lord said' twice, possibly reflecting a slightly different Hebrew or a translator's clarification.

bibcrit_assessment.title: Doubled κύριος hints at expanded Vorlage
bibcrit_assessment.reasoning: The most significant feature is the apparent doubling of יהוה in 'proclaiming the decree of YHWH; YHWH said to me.' MT has only one occurrence; the LXX repetition could reflect either an expansionist Vorlage (consistent with pre-Masoretic plurality of texts) or, more cautiously, a translator's stylistic disambiguation. Without DSS attestation for this verse, the variant remains speculative but methodologically plausible.
bibcrit_assessment.plain: The Greek's repetition of 'Lord' suggests the translator's Hebrew Bible may have included an extra divine name, though this cannot be confirmed without surviving manuscripts.
